A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 24-page versions of the same K-NEWS-STANCE and JOA-ICL paper. Their main text, tables, figures, mathematical formulation, and appendices A.1–A.4 support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Korean and German stance-detection experiments, ablations, segment-level analyses, and news-recommendation and media-bias case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical studies and reports revised numerical results in several appendix tables.

M1.justification: The segment-level stance agent, headline/lead/conclusion/quotation inputs, XML-style label augmentation, and article-level LLM inference remain the same. Revised descriptions and English prompt wording do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Korean article-level and segment-level tasks, German CheeSE evaluation, and six issues for the two case studies. The revised annotation count does not introduce a new population, language, domain, or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: RoBERTa, CoT Embeddings, LKI-BART, PT-HCL, the LLM prompting baselines and agent variants, and Contriever/MMR recommendation comparisons are retained in their corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 revises the reported segment-annotation pool from 19,650 to 21,650. The 999/1,001 article split, CheeSE 800/200/762 split, metrics, model configurations, and prompting/training budgets remain unchanged. This establishes a reported sample-count revision, not additional annotation or experimental reruns.

E4.justification: Table A2 revises the evidence on segment ablation by article genre. For analysis articles, removing quotations changes F1 from 0.649 to 0.669, now exceeding the unchanged unablated 0.663. Table A6 also revises segment-level diagnostic results; the analysis questions and other ablation, error, cost, and case-study designs are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1 retains ten runs, seeds 42–51, and reporting means with standard errors. Annotation-agreement reporting is also unchanged. Revised standard-error values in Table A6 do not constitute a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises quotation statistics, including the total mean from 7.78 to 7.59 and maximum from 45 to 39. Tables A2 and A6 revise several scores: Table A6c's six-shot Gemini-2.0-flash accuracy/F1 changes from 0.580/0.575 to 0.690/0.664. These are reported numerical revisions; the main performance and case-study scores in Tables 3–6 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The article/target/stance-label formulation in Section 3.1 is unchanged. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The headline dataset contribution now claims 21,650 segment annotations rather than 19,650. The additional contribution bullet foregrounds cross-language generalization already claimed in v1's conclusion. The method novelty, comparative-effectiveness, and application claims retain their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning lead importance, quotation difficulty, neutral-segment prediction, and accuracy–cost trade-offs are retained. The limitations concerning language coverage, inference cost, and proof-of-concept case studies are substantively unchanged; reorganized explanatory prose adds no new mechanism or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: Appendices A.1, A.3, and A.4 retain the hardware, software versions, model identifiers, hyperparameters, dataset-access instructions, and prompt templates. English prompt refinements do not change the documented procedure or resource availability.

R1.justification: v3 removes Borges et al. (2019), adds Mohammad et al.'s 2016 dataset paper, and retains the existing SemEval paper as Mohammad et al. (2016b). Section 2 also reclassifies Mets et al. and Lüüsi et al. as sentence-level research rather than full-article research, without substantially changing the paper's overall positioning.

P1.justification: Most edits polish grammar, tense, terminology, and affiliations, with localized rewrites of related work and explanatory passages. v3 expands the contribution list and adds an institutional ethics-approval statement. The section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 moves from PDF page 7 to page 6, and existing tables, captions, and surrounding text undergo spacing and layout adjustments. The figure and table inventory is retained, without a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves readability and reporting. Table 2 corrects the pooled quotation median from 8 to 7, consistent with both split medians, and the ethics statement adds IRB-approval documentation. The main experimental evidence remains unchanged; the unexplained annotation-count and appendix-score revisions do not establish stronger experimental validation.
